title: India's Consumer Regulator Escalates Apple Probe Over iOS 18 Warranty Terms
excerpt: The Central Consumer Protection Authority has ordered a detailed investigation into complaints that the iOS 18 update damaged iPhone screens, leaving users with repair bills of up to Rs 27,900.
body:
• India's Central Consumer Protection Authority has escalated its probe into Apple's software warranty terms to a "detailed investigation" by its investigation wing, after the iPhone maker was formally notified on July 29.
  • The case centres on complaints that the iOS 18 rollout in late 2024 caused green, pink or white lines to appear on iPhone screens, forcing users to pay "exorbitant" sums for repairs because Apple's software licences carry no warranty.
  • Apple is contesting the accusations privately, telling investigators that no warranty on software is in line with global industry standards and that the case rests on just 75 complaints.
  • If found guilty, Apple could face fines — but the larger stakes are potential refunds and changes to its warranty terms in one of its fastest-growing markets.

India's consumer regulator has escalated its investigation into Apple's software warranty terms, ordering a "detailed investigation" into complaints that the iOS 18 update damaged iPhone functionality and left users paying heavily for repairs. The move, confirmed by Reuters through documents seen by the news agency, marks Apple's latest regulatory headache in a market where it is rapidly expanding both manufacturing and sales.

The CCPA last year told Apple it had received a large number of complaints that the iOS 18 rollout in late 2024 led to screen display and microphone malfunctions, forcing customers to pay for repairs because no warranty is provided on software. On July 29 this year, the regulator formally notified Apple it had "escalated" the matter for a "detailed investigation" by its investigation wing.

"The case involves alleged violations of consumer rights," the regulator said in its notice. The escalation signals New Delhi has not been satisfied with Apple's responses.

What users say happened

The investigation covers complaints that green, pink or white lines appeared on users' screens after iOS 18 upgrades. Subsequently, the regulator says, consumers had to pay "exorbitant amounts" for repairs and replacement of display screens, "despite the issues stemming from the company's software upgrade."

https://x.com/Reuters/status/2099795410420105573

The estimated cost of servicing an iPhone 15 screen is 27,900 rupees ($291) — more than a third of the retail price of some models. "Charging consumers for issues arising from the company's own negligence violates the principle of fair trade," the CCPA told Apple, accusing it of violating the rights of "consumers as a class."

Apple's defence

Apple is privately contesting the accusations. In an August 20 reply to investigators, the company said the no-warranty clause was not unusual, noting that consumers were told about it before installation and that it followed lines similar to those of many electronics majors, such as Sony and Samsung.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=kwW97UK2RMg

"A requirement that every issue ... be treated as a breach of an absolute warranty would effectively convert any software provider into an insurer against all technological risk."

— Apple, in its August 20 reply to the CCPA, seen by Reuters

Apple's software licences state the software is provided "without warranty of any kind," with users bearing the entire repair cost if software proves defective; its limited warranty covers hardware only.

Apple also disputed the scale of the problem, saying iOS 18 underwent stringent testing, that the CCPA case was based on just 75 complaints, and that only about 11% of iPhones were still running iOS 18 by June 2026.

Why it matters

If found guilty, Apple may have to pay fines — but the more consequential outcomes could be forced refunds to affected consumers or changes to its business practices in India. The regulator can also ask for changes to Apple's warranty terms, though Reuters notes that would be unprecedented.

The case is not without international precedent. In 2018, Italy sanctioned Apple for failing to advise consumers that the iOS 10 update could adversely affect the performance of older iPhones, and for not offering support to phones out of legal warranty.

India's importance to Apple has only grown. iPhones took a 9% share of the Indian market last year, up from 4% in 2022, according to Counterpoint Research, and the company has been fast expanding iPhone manufacturing in the country. At the same time, it is fending off accusations of breaching domestic antitrust laws — making the CCPA's escalation another front in a lengthening regulatory campaign.

What to watch

The investigation will now examine whether Apple's warranty terms violate India's consumer protection law. Both sides have dug in, which means the dispute could stretch for months. For Indian iPhone owners who paid for post-update screen repairs, the question is whether it ends with refunds; for Apple, whether a key growth market forces it to rewrite warranty terms it applies worldwide.
